PullRequest.Title: sticking the hover verbosity actions to the bottom of the hover provider result

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Uncoalesced synchronous hover scroll handling performs O(P) part traversal and 2V layout-dependent reads plus V positional style writes per update, where V is the number of rendered provider rows offering verbosity controls and P is the number of markdown parts. Writes for one row precede geometry reads for the next, introducing forced style/layout synchronization on the UI thread.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Statically evidenced extra main-thread layout synchronization and JavaScript work while wheel/keyboard scrolling overflowing hovers, with potential scroll jank that grows with event frequency and verbosity-enabled provider rows. No measured timing or user-reported performance symptom is asserted.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: CSS flex-end and position: sticky; bottom: 0 replace the JavaScript scroll callback, eliminating the per-scroll full-part traversal, two synchronous geometry reads per verbosity-enabled row, and corresponding style.top writes without adding provider calls or rebuilding DOM.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: The deleted MarkdownRenderedHoverParts.handleScroll iterated all rendered markdown parts on every hover scrollbar event. For each part with verbosity actions it read hoverElement.offsetTop and clientHeight (base lines 362–363), then wrote actionsContainerInner.style.top (base line 372). The base diff also shows the synchronous forwarding chain DomScrollableElement.onScroll -> ContentHoverWidget._onDidScroll -> ContentHoverWidgetWrapper -> MarkdownHoverParticipant.handleScroll. DomScrollableElement sets native scrollTop before later subscribers run (scrollableElement.ts:739–745), and does not smooth/coalesce mouse-wheel updates (727–732). Thus an overflowing TypeScript hover with verbosity controls ran geometry reads and positional writes on every scroll update; multiple eligible provider rows interleaved reads and writes. This PR deletes that callback chain and uses CSS sticky positioning instead (hover.css:96–97). Blame resolves the removed clientHeight read to commit 8961ff9f680d04110cc19e62384ba1f72554bc41.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open an editor hover by mouse or keyboard, including a TypeScript language-service hover.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Mouse opening retains the existing hover-delay scheduling; keyboard opening starts immediately. Synchronous decoration results can display without waiting for every provider. Provider results arrive in resolve order and rendering/layout must finish to display their rows.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Call extension-host $provideHover with document URI, position and optional verbosity context; return hover contents.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One IPC request per matching extension-backed provider per newly started hover computation, not per markdown string. Providers are invoked concurrently.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical provider count and IPC placement. The diff changes only control positioning and removes scroll-event forwarding.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each returned provider row depends on its IPC response; partial/synchronous hover content can appear earlier.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Ensure per-document tsserver configuration, then execute quickinfo against an existing TypeScript server.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One quickinfo command routed to one syntax/semantic server per TypeScript provider request. Cold or changed document configuration adds one logical configure command, broadcast to the configured server set; unchanged warm configuration adds none.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same quickinfo routing, configuration-cache behavior, server broadcast and per-server request queues.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The TypeScript row waits for ensureConfigurationForDocument and quickinfo. Requests are queued per server; this is not a new process per hover.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Convert provider hover contents and render/sanitize markdown into DOM.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Conversion scales with each successful provider's returned content; rendering runs for nonempty markdown strings in displayed parts, unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same contents were converted and rendered. No new copying, serialization or DOM construction is introduced.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Conversion precedes the response and synchronous markdown rendering precedes row display.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: P matching registered providers, one provider result/row per successful provider, plus decoration parts; markdown size controls rendering cost, not provider-call count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Initial providers start in parallel, with no newly introduced limiter or fan-out. Each tsserver serializes response-bearing synchronous requests through its existing queue. Hover-delay scheduling and cancellation are unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The wrapper suppresses repeated computations for the same anchor/source and cancels superseded operations. HoverAdapter retains at most ten successful previous-hover objects per provider for verbosity context, not as a response memoization cache; empty results are not stored. TypeScript configuration uses a document-keyed promise cache, skips successful unchanged options, retries unsuccessful configuration and removes entries on document close. All unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: provider dispatch, main/extension-host IPC, TypeScript quickinfo/configuration routing and layout call paths were inspected; none are changed.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Extension count, provider duration, TypeScript project size and markdown size vary; no runtime timings were collected.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable introduced regression: provider cardinality, scheduling, content rendering and cold-start boundaries are unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Wheel-scroll, keyboard-scroll or page through an overflowing hover containing verbosity controls.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Native scroll-position updates and browser sticky positioning determine the displayed controls. The removed synchronous event-forwarding chain no longer invokes markdown-part geometry reads and positional writes before scroll handling returns.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Position verbosity controls within their hover row and scroll viewport.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Before: each update traversed P parts, read offsetTop/clientHeight twice per eligible row and wrote style.top once per eligible row. After: zero such JavaScript traversals, geometry reads or top writes; existing control DOM is positioned with CSS sticky.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Scrollbar events synchronously forwarded through the widget and wrapper to every participant; markdown handling interleaved per-row geometry reads and positional writes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Removes synchronous JavaScript and layout-dependent reads from the scroll-event critical path. Browser layout/painting still applies.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: F scroll updates, P rendered markdown parts and V verbosity-enabled provider rows, where V is at most the number of provider results, not the number of markdown paragraphs.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: DomScrollableElement performs immediate native scroll updates and disables wheel smooth scrolling. Previously the added participant handler ran synchronously on each event; now the browser owns sticky positioning without that callback.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No provider request, markdown rerender or resource fetch is triggered by scrolling before or after the diff. Existing hover DOM and provider results are reused; there is no new cache or retained collection.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the entire removed callback chain and native scroll update ordering were inspected. The removed mechanism is concrete; its performance benefit is statically evidenced rather than benchmarked.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact layout synchronization duration and frequency of multiple verbosity-enabled provider rows are unmeasured.
Scenarios.Verdict: No introduced regression. The PR removes a concrete synchronous scroll-work regression; introducing-commit provenance was recorded through report_regression_fix.

Scenarios.Scenario: Increase or decrease hover verbosity once or repeatedly, for an explicit row or the selected markdown-row range.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing action invokes the hover command, waits for each supported provider in the chosen range, replaces that row's children and disposables, then notifies contents changed for relayout/focus. Async code highlighting may finish later.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Request updated hover content with verbosityDelta and the previous-hover identifier.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per supported extension-backed provider row in the chosen range. The caller awaits rows sequentially; it is not a request per markdown string.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical support checks, range selection, sequential awaits and IPC count. Previous hover content was already represented by its identifier across IPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each replacement waits for its provider. Completing the whole range precedes the final contents-changed notification.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Execute quickinfo at the requested verbosity level, after ensuring document configuration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One quickinfo on the routed TypeScript server per supported TypeScript row. Warm unchanged document configuration adds no configure request; cold/changed configuration uses the existing shared configure routing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same quickinfo and optional configure operations at the same point in the command.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The TypeScript replacement waits for this operation; server request queues remain unchanged.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Render new markdown/control nodes, collect the new row's children and replace the existing row's children.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One replacement per successful supported-row update, proportional to returned markdown and direct child count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same renderer, child-array allocation, replacement and disposal ran previously. The diff removes only an actions-container reference from the rendered-part wrapper.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous DOM construction/replacement precedes final hover relayout.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: S supported rows in the chosen range, up to P provider rows; one explicit row gives at most one request. Repeated commands can overlap and use the existing provider-keyed cancellation/delta accumulation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Rows in one update command are processed sequentially. Separate commands may overlap; the existing per-provider operation map cancels prior tokens but is not a global concurrency limiter. Neither behavior changes.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Previous-hover lookup uses the unchanged ten-entry provider map; it is not an extra read of all provider state. Ongoing requests are canceled per provider and verbosity deltas accumulated. New children are acquired before old disposables are released, preserving existing resource reuse. No new negative-cache behavior or lifetime expansion.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: command-range loop, per-provider request handling, previous-hover IPC conversion, replacement and disposal were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Number of supported providers, rapid command frequency and returned-content size vary. Providers' responsiveness to cancellation is extension-specific.
Scenarios.Verdict: No introduced performance regression: request frequency, effective concurrency, allocation and disposal are unchanged; CSS positioning replaces dependence on scroll callbacks.

Scenarios.Scenario: Display or update rich hover markdown containing code blocks, images or registered-filesystem media.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Initial sanitized markdown can display before asynchronous code highlighting and media loads complete. Those completions invoke the existing contents-changed callback and relayout; the diff does not add an await for them.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve a cold language tokenizer and load grammar resources through the existing extension-resource loader before highlighting code.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Code rendering is invoked per code block, but tokenizer creation is coalesced per registered language factory; warm support adds no factory initialization. Cold grammar loading depends on that language's grammar dependencies, not paragraph count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical markdown renderer and lazy tokenization path with the same factory-promise reuse.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the initial hover-display critical path; highlighting completion triggers the existing callback and relayout.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Set image/media source URLs for browser loading.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Source setup occurs per media element; actual network retrieval depends on distinct URLs and existing browser caching. This PR introduces no new elements or repeated source assignment.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same media elements, source rewriting and load callbacks.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Media loading does not block initial row display; image load callbacks subsequently request relayout.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read registered-filesystem media for a resource transport or scoped object URL.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: In object-URL mode, one read per cold distinct URI shared by concurrent references, with microtask-deferred last-reference cleanup. Transport mode retains the existing endpoint/browser-cache behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same resource resolution, read count, shared promises and reference disposal. The diff preserves the existing markdown disposables.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only that media's display waits for the read; hover text remains independently displayable.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: B code blocks, L distinct cold language tokenization factories and U distinct media resource URIs. Multiple references to an object-URL resource share an acquisition promise while retained.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Code blocks render asynchronously and are joined by the existing Promise.all before code placeholders are replaced. Independent media URIs resolve concurrently; same-URI object-URL acquisition is coalesced. The diff changes none of this.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Tokenization support and pending initialization are reused per language; resolved unsupported factories are not retried until registration changes. Browser media caches are unchanged. Registered object URLs are URI-keyed, share pending promises, and release/revoke after the last reference; failures release their reference. No new cache keys or retention.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for unchanged ownership and scheduling: markdown callbacks, tokenizer promise reuse, media rewriting and filesystem object-URL acquisition/disposal were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large markdown, external media latency, grammar dependencies and host-specific filesystem transports vary; no execution or profiling was performed.
Scenarios.Verdict: No introduced eager work, boundary fan-out or resource retention: richer content follows exactly the existing rendering and resource paths.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resize, replace, hide and dispose a hover across repeated editor interactions.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Resize and contents changes retain the existing synchronous dimension measurements, scrollbar scan and editor layout. Replacing/hiding disposes rendered content, and editor-widget disposal releases the widget and listeners. CSS determines control placement without new lifecycle work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Measure DOM dimensions, scan scrolling bounds and relayout the editor content widget.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing measurements per resize/content-change event remain. Scrollbar dimension events no longer invoke the deleted per-markdown-row scroll handler.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same measurement/layout entry points, plus scroll-event participant forwarding when scrollbar dimensions or position changed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous on resize/relayout as before; the diff removes a downstream callback rather than adding another layout pass.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number and size of currently rendered parts and frequency of resize/content-change events; retained hover resources remain bounded by the active rendered content and existing provider caches.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: UI layout and disposal run synchronously on the main thread. Outstanding hover-operation tokens are canceled on existing disposal paths. Removing emitter/listener registrations reduces retained listener state.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing active rendered content and per-part disposables are replaced/disposed. The removed actions-container field was only a DOM reference, not a disposal owner; all markdown/action DisposableStores remain owned and disposed. No lazy resource becomes eager or loses cleanup.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: resize/show/hide paths, rendered-part ownership and action/markdown stores were inspected; lifecycle ownership is preserved.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact browser flex/sticky layout cost versus previous relative positioning is unmeasured. No concrete mechanism establishes a regression from the added CSS alone.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: no added relayout entry point, larger retained object graph or missing cleanup. The added browser test constructs and finally disposes its DOM/store without changing production scheduling.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass over all six changed files and every diff page against base 184833947d794fddbe2cda93f3ad318c42724f55. No high-confidence introduced performance regressions found. Traced opening, scrolling, verbosity updates, rich-markdown boundaries and hover lifecycle. Recorded the concrete removed scroll geometry/write mechanism and its introducing commit as internal regression-fix data. Static review only; runtime browser timings and arbitrary third-party provider internals remain unmeasured.
